BinFill.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    placed
        Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), write placed=[] explicitly: the field is always output as an explicit list, even when empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Write the list as a JSON array with double-quoted strings, never Python-style single quotes; the field is compared literally. e.g. ["green", "green"]
    cubes
        Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each as [color, [y, x]]. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), list every visible cube of a goal color ordered by distance to the point 10 px to the larger-x side of the reported bin center ([bin_y, bin_x + 10]), nearest first (ties: smaller y); do not order by the reported bin center itself. Otherwise copy the carried-in list and: remove an entry only if the execution steps shown at THIS step include the fingers closing (about 100% to about 46% open) within about 10 px of that entry and the cube then reported 'held in the gripper'; if the shown steps begin with a cube already held, remove nothing for it. Then for every goal-color detection in the shown steps (excluding the one marked 'held in the gripper', any detection within about 10 px of the held cube's position while it is held, and any detection within about 10 px of the reported bin center), match detections to entries ONE-TO-ONE in each frame: an entry takes the nearest detection within about 10 px and only that one, keeping its slot and taking that newest position; any further detection within 10 px of that entry but with no other unmatched entry within about 10 px is a new cube and is appended at the end, in order of first appearance; a detection about 10 px or more from every carried entry is a new cube and is appended likewise. Example: carried [["red", [58, 160]]] and a frame showing red at [60, 163] and [67, 167] becomes [["red", [60, 163]], ["red", [67, 167]]]. A cube reported 20 px or more from the bin center is a real table cube and is entered even if it showed up just after a release; a cube that vanishes for a frame or two because the arm covers it keeps its entry and is not re-added. Never reorder entries, never drop-and-re-append: the list order is the age order and nothing seen later changes it. Example of a refresh: carried [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [71, 154]]] with a green reported at [68, 160] becomes [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [68, 160]]]. Cubes of colors not named in the goal are never entered. Write it as a JSON array with double-quoted color strings. e.g. [["blue", [54, 118]], ["blue", [87, 181]]]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, choose the color this way: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again (a color once started is finished before any other color is touched); only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start with the color of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) whose color is still needed. Do not choose the start color by required count or by a fixed color preference. Among the cubes of that color, point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color, with no distance condition of any kind; a cube is never skipped for being near the bin. If the scene at this decision step shows a detection of that color within about 10 px of that entry, point at that detection's center; if not (the arm may be covering it), point at the remembered position. The order of `cubes` is the only criterion among same-colored cubes: do not choose the cube nearest the gripper, nearest the button, nearest or farthest from the bin, or the one with the smallest y. The target is the detection of that color within about 10 px of the chosen entry in the scene at this decision step; a detection that has drifted a few pixels is still the same cube, so do not discard it, and never point at a detection lying within about 10 px of the bin center. At step #1 the first entry of `cubes` is the needed-color cube nearest the point 10 px to the larger-x side of the reported bin center, as ordered when `cubes` is filled. A point offset by a pixel or two from the detection center is acceptable; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first entry of `cubes` whose color is still needed, and if `cubes` has no such entry, choose A pointing at any visible cube of a needed color, or failing that any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

ButtonUnmask.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    picks_done
        Number of container pick-ups completed. Start at 0. Look only at the scene at this decision step itself (the last observed step, after all execution steps). If that scene shows a container held in the gripper, write carried-in value + 1. Otherwise copy the carried-in value unchanged, even if earlier execution steps at this decision step showed a container held before it was released. e.g. 1
    goal_cube_positions
        Ordered list of the [y, x] positions of the cubes the goal instruction names, in the goal's order. If this step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere (the scene before the button is pressed), read the goal, take each cube it names in order, and write that cube's [y, x] as shown; skip cubes the goal does not name. Otherwise copy the carried-in list unchanged; never overwrite an entry from a cube briefly exposed under a lifted container. e.g. [[78, 157], [106, 105]] when the goal names blue then red.

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    An episode starts in A (press the button): the first step shows the three loose cubes and no containers. Rule 1: if the step shows loose cubes and no containers anywhere and nothing held, choose A (press the button); at the same time record goal_cube_positions: the [y, x] of each cube the goal names, in the goal's order. Rule 2: if the step shows containers on the table and the gripper is NOT holding a container, choose B (pick up the container). The target position is the entry of goal_cube_positions at index picks_done (first entry when picks_done is 0, second entry when picks_done is 1). Point at the center of the container nearest to that recorded position, writing the point as [y, x]. Ignore containers that cover no recorded position. Rule 3: if the step shows a container held in the gripper, choose C (put down the container). After that, Rule 2 applies again with the next cube in the goal. If all cubes named in the goal have already been picked (picks_done equals the number of cubes named), choose C if holding, otherwise B at the container nearest the last entry of goal_cube_positions. Unforeseen situation: if a container is held, choose C; if containers are visible and nothing is held, choose B at the container nearest the entry of goal_cube_positions at index picks_done (the last entry if picks_done is beyond the list); if no containers are visible, choose A.

ButtonUnmaskSwap.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    buttons_pressed
        Carried-in count plus 1 if any execution frame shown at this step either reports a button 'is pressed down' or shows the gripper within a few pixels of a button's listed position at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed (two containers gliding and swapping in neighbouring frames confirms the same press); otherwise the carried-in count. Count at most one press per step. Start at 0. e.g. 1
    green_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the green cube. If a frame shows the green cube uncovered and no containers, write the cube's position. In the step where containers appear, the field becomes the position of the container standing on the carried-in green position, even if that container never moves. Then follow that container through the frames shown: match each container to the nearest container in the previous frame; during a button press two containers glide around each other and finish swapped, so after the press the green container sits where the other moving container started. Write its position in the last frame shown. Once a frame shows the green cube exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, write the cube's last visible position and freeze the field; a container later set down over the cube does not update it. Start with the cube position seen at the first step. e.g. [136, 108]
    red_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the red cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position before containers exist; from the step where containers appear, the container standing on the carried-in position (even one that never moves), followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown; once the red cube is seen exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, the cube's last visible position, frozen regardless of any container later set down over it. e.g. [100, 166]
    blue_container
        [y, x] of the container hiding the blue cube, kept exactly as green_container: cube position before containers exist; from the step where containers appear, the container standing on the carried-in position (even one that never moves), followed frame to frame (two movers during a press swap places), written at the last frame shown; once the blue cube is seen exposed beneath a container held in the gripper, the cube's last visible position, frozen regardless of any container later set down over it. e.g. [120, 181]
    picked_colors
        Carried-in list; append the color of the cube that appears beneath a container shown 'held in the gripper' among this step's frames, if that color is not already in the list. Start empty. e.g. ["green"]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Start every episode in A (press the first button). First update memory for this step (in particular buttons_pressed, using the press signs named in the memory instruction: the phrase 'is pressed down', or the gripper on a button at height 0.035 or lower with fingers closed, usually with two containers swapping). Then apply the first matching rule: 1. If buttons_pressed is 0: A. 2. If buttons_pressed is 1: B. 3. If the scene at this decision step shows a container 'held in the gripper': D (put down the container). 4. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, and picked_colors is empty: C, pointing at the memory position (<color>_container) of the FIRST cube color named in the goal instruction (the one after 'hiding the'). Use the remembered container position, not the cube's original spot. 5. If buttons_pressed is 2, nothing is held, picked_colors has one entry, and the goal names a second cube ('another container hiding the ...'): C, pointing at the memory position of that SECOND color. This is the container that has not been lifted yet; do not point at the one just put down. 6. If every cube named in the goal is already in picked_colors and nothing is held: the task is done; answer D. Fallback: if the needed color's memory position is unknown, point C at the container nearest that cube's last known position; if no rule fits at all, answer the next unfinished item in goal order (A, B, C, D).

MoveCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    method
        The way the demonstration moved the cube. At the first decision step, read it from the demonstration steps. Do not decide from the first frame in which the fingers close; look at the transport frames (those in which the cube is sliding or carried toward the target) and at the greatest height the gripper reaches while anything is marked as held. A one-frame finger reading of roughly 19-30% that drops to about 0% at the next frame is just the fingers closing on nothing, not a grasp. `pick` if the cube is marked as held in the gripper while the gripper is well above the table (height above about 0.08) with fingers partly closed (about 40-60% open) and the cube is then released over the target; `hook` if the fingers settle at about 20-25% and stay there through the transport frames, the stick (peg) is explicitly marked as held in the gripper, and the gripper rises above about 0.08 carrying the stick before dragging it against the cube toward the target; `push` if in the transport frames the fingers read about 0% and the gripper height stays below about 0.04 the whole time, and nothing is ever marked as held while the gripper is raised; this holds even if the gripper came down beside the stick, the stick's head is listed next to the gripper, or the stick sits somewhere else at the end because the gripper pushed it aside. At every later step copy the value carried in unchanged; never write `unknown` after the first step. e.g. hook

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL

An episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory, fingers fully open and nothing executed yet; first fill `method` from the demonstration steps, judging it from the transport frames (the cube moving toward the target) and the greatest height the gripper reaches while something is marked as held, never from one finger reading during the closing motion (a brief 19-30% that drops to 0% is closing on nothing, so a demonstration that brushed the stick while pushing is still `push`), then choose by it: `push` -> C, `pick` -> D, `hook` -> A. At every later decision step, what is in the fingers is read from the step itself: the execution steps shown since the previous decision (descent, finger closure, rise) and the finger opening and gripper height in the scene at this step. In these execution steps judge by finger opening and the rise rather than by whether an object is marked as held, since the marking at a decision step can be absent; this applies to the robot's own execution steps only, not to the demonstration, where the held marking is one of the cues that separates `hook` and `pick` from `push`. Rules, applied in whatever situation the policy stands in: - If `method` is `push`: choose C (close gripper and push the cube to the target). This is the only subgoal for a push episode. - If the fingers are now closed to about 40-60% and the gripper has risen after descending onto the cube: choose E (place the cube onto the target). - If the fingers are now closed to about 20-25% and the gripper has risen after descending onto the stick: choose B (hook the cube to the target with the peg). - Otherwise (fingers fully open, or closed to about 0% with nothing raised; this covers the first decision step once `method` has been filled, and any later decision step after a grasp attempt that closed on nothing or reopened) choose by `method`: `pick` -> D (pick up the cube), `hook` -> A (pick up the peg), `push` -> C. `method` is the only record of the demonstration, which is never shown again; it is read exactly here. PatternLock.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    plan
        The ordered list of menu letters the demonstration traces. If this step shows DEMONSTRATION STEPS (the first step, memory empty), build it now and never change it afterwards: the cell highlighted at demo t=0 is the start, whether it is labelled 'highlighted target' or 'highlighted area' (either label counts, its coordinates are used exactly as the start, and it adds no letter itself); each time a different target becomes highlighted in the demo frames, take dy = new y minus previous highlighted y and dx = new x minus previous highlighted x (coordinates at the frame it first appears). |dy| >= 8 with dy > 0 means forward, dy < 0 means backward; |dx| >= 8 with dx > 0 means left, dx < 0 means right; both over threshold means the diagonal (forward=A, backward=B, left=C, right=D, forward-left=E, forward-right=F, backward-left=G, backward-right=H). One letter per newly highlighted target, in demo order. A short demonstration with only one newly highlighted target gives a one-letter list, e.g. ["B"]; that is a complete, valid plan. Never write 'unknown' or an empty value; whenever a demonstration is shown the plan has at least one letter. If the step shows no demonstration, copy the carried-in plan character for character. Write the list exactly as a JSON array with double-quoted uppercase letters, square brackets, comma-space separated: ["C", "E", "C", "G"], never ['C', 'E', 'C', 'G'], never without brackets, never with spaces inside the quotes. e.g. ["E", "D", "G", "H"]
    moves_done
        How many planned moves have been finished by the scene at this step. Write 0 when the step shows demonstration steps and the carried memory is empty (first step). Otherwise the step shows execution steps of one completed move, so write the carried-in moves_done plus one. e.g. 2

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Every episode starts at the first decision step with empty memory and the demonstration shown; the subgoal there is the first letter of the plan just built from the demonstration (plan[0]). At every later decision step (memory carried in, no demonstration shown), first compute one number n = carried moves_done + 1. n is the count of planned moves finished so far, including the one the execution steps just showed, and it is also exactly the moves_done value written at this step; these are the same number, not two different ones, so never add one to n again. The execution steps just completed plan[n - 1]; the subgoal is plan[n] (0-based), the letter immediately after the one just completed. Self-check from what the step shows: the direction the gripper travelled from the first shown execution frame to the scene at this decision step (same dy/dx rule as the plan) must equal plan[n - 1]; the subgoal is the letter right after it in the plan, never plan[n - 1] again (unless the plan genuinely repeats it) and never plan[n + 1]. So the first step performs plan[0]; the second step (carried moves_done = 0, n = 1) performs plan[1]; the third step (carried moves_done = 1, n = 2) performs plan[2]; and so on: the k-th decision step of the episode performs plan[k - 1]. No subgoal needs a point. After a move finishes, the next decision step always advances to the next plan letter regardless of where the gripper ended; never repeat or skip. If n (carried moves_done + 1) is at or beyond the length of the plan (nothing remains), repeat the last plan letter. If the plan could not be built (no demonstration visible and empty plan), derive the direction from the two highlighted targets currently visible if there are two (direction from the older-looking one near the gripper to the other, same dy/dx rule), otherwise choose A: move forward. In any other unforeseen situation, pick plan[n] with n = carried moves_done + 1 if it exists (plan[0] when memory is empty), else A.

    pending_cubes
        Ordered list of [y, x] of cubes on highlighted white areas not yet picked up. Start with `[]`. When the execution steps shown at this step list `highlighted area` positions (they appear right after the button press and vanish before the decision step), write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area (as seen in that same execution step), and order the entries by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last). Colour plays no part and the order the areas are printed in plays no part. e.g. cubes at [57, 141], [70, 166], [92, 85] -> [[92, 85], [57, 141], [70, 166]]. Otherwise copy the list carried in, keeping its order; if the execution steps shown at this step show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper' (the gripper descended to ~0.02 height and the fingers closed to ~46%), remove the one entry whose [y, x] is nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted, whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry in its order. Keep the list unchanged on a step that only shows a placing (fingers reopen to 100%, cube left on table). e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

    The episode starts in A (press button). Rules, applied to whatever situation you are in: 1. If button_pressed is `no` (or memory is empty) and no execution step in front of you shows the button pressed down: choose A, press button. 2. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step). On the button-press step itself (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) there is no carried-in list: point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most, colour ignored), using that cube's current position, or the highlighted-area position from the execution step when the cube is not listed in the scene. To locate the stored entry in the scene: point at the visible cube that lies within about 15 px of the stored entry if there is one; if no listed cube is within that radius (the gripper hovering above a cube often hides it from the object list), point at the stored entry itself, or at that cube's position in the most recent execution step where it was listed near the stored entry. If the scene at this decision step (or the last execution steps) shows a cube held in the gripper (fingers ~46% open, cube marked 'is held in the gripper'): choose C, place the cube onto the table. 3. If the gripper is empty (fingers open, no cube held) and button_pressed is `yes` (or this step's execution steps showed the button pressed down) and pending_cubes (after this step's update) is non-empty: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step). On the button-press step itself (the step whose execution steps list highlighted areas) there is no carried-in list: point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (the highlighted cube with the smallest x, the robot's right-most, colour ignored), using that cube's current position, or the highlighted-area position from the execution step when the cube is not listed in the scene. To locate the stored entry in the scene: point at the visible cube that lies within about 15 px of the stored entry if there is one; if no listed cube is within that radius (the gripper hovering above a cube often hides it from the object list), point at the stored entry itself, or at that cube's position in the most recent execution step where it was listed near the stored entry. Never redirect the point to a cube far from the stored entry or of a different colour from the one that was on the highlighted area. The list is consumed from its front; an entry leaves the list by matching the cube that was grasped, never by its place in the list. 4. If pending_cubes is empty, the gripper is empty, and button_pressed is `yes`: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op. 5. Any situation not covered: if a cube is held choose C; else if any cube position is remembered in the carried-in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

Colour plays no part and the order the areas are printed in plays no part. e.g. cubes at [57, 141], [70, 166], [92, 85] -> [[92, 85], [57, 141], [70, 166]]. PickXtimes.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    placements_done
        Integer count of completed placements of the goal-colored cube onto the target. Start at 0 on the first step. At each decision step, take the value carried in; add 1 if the execution steps shown at this step contain the cube marked 'is held in the gripper' and then, later in the same step, the fingers opened to about 100% with the gripper low (height below about 0.03) and the cube now lying at roughly the target's position, no longer held. Otherwise keep the carried value unchanged. Never decrease it. e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    First read the goal instruction to get the required number of placements N: if it says 'repeating this action two times' N=2, 'three times' N=3, and so on; if it mentions no repetition, N=1. The cube to use is the one whose color the goal names (ignore other cubes). Update placements_done first, then decide. An episode starts in subgoal A (pick up the cube). Rules, applied in whatever situation you are in: 1. If the goal-colored cube is shown 'is held in the gripper' at the scene of this decision step (fingers about 46% open, gripper raised), choose B: place the cube onto the target. 2. If the cube is NOT held at the scene of this decision step (fingers ~100% open) and placements_done (after this step's update) is less than N, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the current [y, x] of the goal-colored cube as shown in the final scene of this step (after a placement it will be sitting on or near the target; point at the cube, not the target). 3. If the cube is NOT held and placements_done (after this step's update) is equal to or greater than N, choose C: press the button to stop. 4. If the gripper closed but the cube is not reported as held (a missed grasp), treat it as not held: apply rule 2 or 3 by placements_done. If you meet a situation none of these rules cover, default to: if the cube is held choose B; otherwise if placements_done < N choose A pointing at the goal-colored cube's current position; otherwise choose C.

RouteStick.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    demo_moves
        If the memory carried in is empty (first decision step), read the DEMONSTRATION STEPS and write one menu letter per leg, in order. A leg runs from one highlighted target to the first frame where a different target is highlighted (the gripper has reached the next target). For each leg: new target x smaller than the previous target x means RIGHT, larger means LEFT. Gripper y at the middle frames of the leg smaller than the y of the stick (cube) between the two targets means it passed the BACKWARD side, larger means FORWARD. LEFT+backward=A, RIGHT+forward=B, LEFT+forward=C, RIGHT+backward=D. At every later step copy the list carried in unchanged. Write the list exactly as a Python-style list of single-quoted uppercase letters separated by a comma and a space, no other characters. e.g. ['D', 'B', 'C']
    legs_done
        Write 0 if the memory carried in is empty (first decision step). Otherwise write the carried-in legs_done plus 1, because every decision step after the first shows one completed execution leg (the gripper moved and a different target became highlighted). e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The episode starts with the first letter of demo_moves. At the first decision step (carried-in memory empty) write legs_done=0 and issue demo_moves[0] (zero-based). At every later decision step issue demo_moves[carried-in legs_done + 1]: the index is the legs_done you write at this step, never the carried-in number. The leg visible in the execution steps of this decision step is demo_moves[carried-in legs_done]; it is already finished and is never issued again. The letter to issue is always the one after it. Before answering, check that the letter you issue is not the letter describing the movement you just watched in the execution steps (its direction and side, read as in the demonstration); if it is, you have used the carried-in index and must move one index further. Worked line: carried-in legs_done=3 -> the observed leg was demo_moves[3] (already done) -> write legs_done=4 -> issue demo_moves[4]. No option needs a point. The letters mean: A = move to the nearest left target (larger x) passing on the backward side (smaller y) of the stick; B = nearest right target (smaller x) passing on the forward side (larger y); C = nearest left target passing on the forward side; D = nearest right target passing on the backward side. If legs_done is beyond the end of demo_moves, or demo_moves is missing, re-derive what you can: if the demonstration is visible, rebuild the list from it; otherwise repeat the last letter in demo_moves, and if there is none, issue A.

StopCube.policy_prompt:
THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    crossings
        Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the side of the carried-in scene_frame (smaller_x if its cube_x < its target_x, else larger_x; skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2
    first_cross_t
        Carry it unchanged if it is already set. If it is empty and the crossings count you just computed at this step is 1 or more, find the first consecutive pair in this step's side sequence whose side differs; the earlier member is either the carried-in scene_frame or a frame of this step, the later member is a frame of this step. With t1, t2 their timesteps, d1 = cube_x - target_x at the earlier frame (its own target_x) and d2 likewise at the later frame, write t1 + (t2 - t1) * |d1| / (|d1| + |d2|), rounded half up to a whole timestep. Never extrapolate; the carried-in scene_frame always supplies the frame before a flip that precedes this step's first frame. Otherwise leave it empty. e.g. 30
    scene_frame
        Write the ordered list [timestep, cube_x, target_x] of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step it is the t=0 frame. The side of the target line for any frame is smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, else larger_x; the carried-in scene_frame gives the side, timestep and positions of the last frame of the previous step, and is the frame before the flip whenever a crossing lies between the previous scene and this step's first frame. e.g. [56, 104, 117]

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away, so the press, which takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, scene_frame, first_cross_t; the crossing that brings crossings to N-1 often happens inside the frames of the very step where the decision is made), then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values alone: - Predict the timing. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Do not read the cube's direction or speed from the frames to make the decision: cube speed varies threefold across episodes and changes around the turnaround, and the predicted arrival time computed from first_cross_t decides on its own. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if and only if crossings == N-1 AND remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, so it is started once the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away). Whether the cube is still running out, stopped at its turnaround, or already heading back toward the target makes no difference: being past the turnaround or moving back is not enough while remaining > 30. No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while remaining > 30, whatever the cube is doing (the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding; the cube on its way out to the far end; the cube stopped at the turnaround; and the cube already past the turnaround and heading back toward the target, as long as more than 30 timesteps remain). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately. Never choose A after the first step.

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    visits_done
        Carry in the previous value (start at 0 on the first step, where memory is empty). Add 1 if and only if the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) shows the cube 'held in the gripper' AND a 'highlighted target' is listed in that scene. Do NOT consult the earlier execution frames of this step; it does not matter whether they already showed the highlight. Otherwise keep the carried-in value unchanged: if no highlighted target is listed (pick-up just ended), or the cube is not held (put-down ended with fingers fully open and the cube resting on the table, or the press-button step), the value does not change. Write the updated value; it is the value the subgoal rules read at this step. e.g. 3

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    Coordinates are [y, x]. The right-side target is the one with the SMALLER x; the left-side target is the one with the LARGER x. First read the goal to get the required number of target visits REQ: if it says 'repeating this back and forth motion N times' then REQ = 2*N (two=4, three=6); if it instead says 'then put it down on the left-side target' then REQ = 2. Every episode starts with subgoal A. Before applying the rules, compute this step's UPDATED visits_done exactly as the memory instruction says (carried-in value, plus 1 if the current scene shows the cube held AND a highlighted target). Every comparison with REQ below refers to that updated value, never to the carried-in value. Rules (apply whichever matches the current step and the updated memory): 1. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and visits_done is 0 (cube resting on the table, fingers open, nothing done yet): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the cube's center coordinates. 2. If the cube IS held in the gripper and updated visits_done < REQ: choose B, move to the top of the target, pointing at the target that is NOT highlighted in the current scene, using that target's listed coordinates. If neither target is highlighted (right after the pick-up), point at the right-side target, the one with the smaller x. 3. If the cube IS held in the gripper and updated visits_done >= REQ (the cube is now above the left-side target after the last required visit): choose C, put the cube on the table. 4. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and updated visits_done >= REQ (cube resting on the table after the put-down, fingers fully open, gripper raised): choose D, press the button. If no rule matches: when the cube is held, choose B pointing at the target that is not highlighted; when the cube is on the table and visits_done is 0, choose A at the cube; when the cube is on the table and visits_done > 0, choose D.

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR MEMORY
    picks_done
        Count of completed pick-ups. Write 0 at the first decision step (memory empty). At any later step, look only at the gripper in the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step): if it is raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%), write the carried value plus one, no matter what the cube list says (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position); if the fingers are 100% open, copy the carried value unchanged even if a cube line says 'lifted off the table'. e.g. 1

THE POLICY PROMPT FOR SUBGOAL
    The number of required pick-ups comes from the goal instruction: 'pick up ... again' means 1 pick-up; 'for two times' means 2 pick-ups; 'three times' means 3 pick-ups. An episode starts in subgoal A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube the demonstration grasped. The point for A is never taken from memory; it is found from what the step shows, by the point rule at the end of this instruction. The memory holds only picks_done. Rules, applied at every decision step after updating memory: - The robot is holding the cube if and only if the scene at this decision step shows the gripper raised (height about 0.12 or more) with fingers partly closed (about 46-51%, not 100%); the cube list is irrelevant to this test (the held cube may still be listed at its old table position), and fingers 100% open means not holding regardless of any 'lifted off the table' line. Holding: choose B: put it down. - Otherwise (fingers 100% open): if picks_done is less than the required number of pick-ups, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the cube given by the point rule below; if picks_done equals or exceeds the required number, choose C: press the button to finish. Point rule for A. At the first decision step (memory empty), use the demonstration steps shown at that step: find the demonstration frame where the gripper is lowest (height about 0.02) with fingers about 46-51% open; the grasped cube is the listed cube (from a demonstration frame before the gripper descended) nearest that gripper position, and it is the cube reported 'held in the gripper' in the following frames. Ignore cubes that vanish from the list earlier while the gripper is high and 100% open; they are only hidden by the arm. After the demonstration's put-down, follow that cube through the shuffle to the last demonstration frame, tracking jointly rather than frame by frame. (1) The shuffle frames are the consecutive demonstration frames, after the gripper has parked high and 100% open, in which cube positions change by more than a few px. (2) Any cube that keeps the same position (within a few px) through a stretch of shuffle frames is resting during that stretch and is excluded from the matching there; the moving cubes in a stretch are the ones to be assigned (a different pair of cubes may move in a later stretch while the previously moving cube rests). (3) Assign the moving listed cubes in each shuffle frame one-to-one to the tracked moving cubes (never two tracked cubes to one listed cube), and choose, over the whole run of shuffle frames, the single consistent assignment whose total frame-to-frame displacement, summed over all moving cubes and all frames, is smallest. Do not decide each frame on its own: per-frame distances to the two candidates are often nearly equal (differences of a few px or less), a cube can jump 20-30 px between frames, lists are sorted by y, not identity, and the moving cubes may or may not have swapped places by the end (both outcomes occur), so do not assume the grasped cube returns to its old spot and do not assume it ends elsewhere. (4) The grasped cube's position in the last demonstration frame under that assignment is its last position. Point at the cube in the scene at the start of execution nearest its last demonstration position. At every later decision step where A is chosen, the execution steps shown contain the put-down descent: the frame where the gripper is at table height (below about 0.04) with the fingers opening; point at the listed cube in the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown) nearest that descent position, since that is the cube just set down and the cube to pick again. Pointing at the listed cube position, or within a few px of it (such as the demonstration's grasp position), is acceptable. Never point at any other cube.
